2. Humanities, Social and Behavioral Sciences,  24 semester hours is required in areas of humanities (English, History, Classics, Foreign Language, Philosophy, Arts, etc), social science (Sociology, Economics, Political Science, Anthropology, etc.)  and behavioral science (Psychology, etc.).  

3. Additional Required course work will include at least two writing-intensive courses, which can be in the humanities or the social/behavioral sciences and may be counted as part of the 24-semester hour requirement for the humanities and social sciences. Please note: 
AP or IB credit acceptable to the student's undergraduate college is allowed for a maximum of twelve (12) credits. AP and IB credits must be documented on an official transcript.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine considers diversity a core component of medical education. We are committed to supporting learners via one-on-one mentoring, recruitment and retention of a diverse student body, and sponsoring activities to increase diversity. To learn more about our community, we encourage applicants to visit https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/diversity. If you have any questions or need additional guidance, please don't hesitate to email somdiversity@jhmi.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Excused absences may be granted in cases of illness, religious observance, family emergency, presentations at scientific conferences, or required legal activity (e.g., jury duty) through discussion (in advance whenever feasible) with the section director, course director, and/or Associate Dean for Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: We believe that creating medicine’s next great leaders is about more than just academics and time in the classroom. The Johns Hopkins School of Medicine offers our students the rare opportunity to live and study in an urban environment at the heart of Baltimore, within one of the world’s leading centers of medical advancement and scientific innovation. We enjoy seeing our passionate and diverse student body grow professionally and personally as they soak up all that Baltimore and the Johns Hopkins Hospital have to offer.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The School of Medicine is located in East Baltimore, 20 minutes by car from the undergraduate campus and a short walk from the Inner Harbor. The medical campus includes the Schools of Public Health and Nursing, as well as Johns Hopkins Hospital. The 44-acre campus is accessible by subway, and a free Johns Hopkins shuttle service is available for students, faculty, and employees. Useful information for day-to-day life on the School of Medicine campus is available on our website: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/som/life-at-hopkins/campus-life
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The Housing Office helps students, house staff, postdoctoral fellows, staff, and faculty at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine and School of Nursing, Bloomberg School of Public Health, The Johns Hopkins Hospital, and Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center with their off-campus accommodations. Their primary focus is assisting those looking to relocate to the Baltimore area. Please visit the Housing website for more information: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/som/life-at-hopkins/housing
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Johns Hopkins offers support to gender and sexual minorities through formal programs and organizations, including the American Medical Women's Association, the Women in Surgery Interest Group, the Women's Health Interest Group, and the Gertrude Stein Society. Our staff also supports and counsels the many diverse students who attend our medical school.  If you have any questions or need additional guidance, please don't hesitate to email somdiversity@jhmi.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The University has procedures in place to assist students with disabilities. A full description of the range of services is available through the Office of Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action at https://oie.jhu.edu/ada-compliance-and-disability-accommodations/.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Johns Hopkins has exceptional support systems, programs, and resources for our students across eight facets of well-being: emotional and mental, physical, social, sexual, spiritual, financial, environmental, and professional. To learn more about the different services, please visit:https://wellbeing.jhu.edu/.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
At Johns Hopkins, our campus culture thrives on collaboration, innovation, and a shared commitment to cultivating tomorrow's medical leaders today. From our interdisciplinary research centers to our community health initiatives, we offer students an environment that encourages curiosity, fosters inclusivity, and promotes lifelong learning.

As a student here, you’ll join a community of aspiring physicians and scientists who are passionate about making an impact. Our small class sizes and supportive faculty ensure that you’ll build strong connections with peers and mentors alike. Outside of the classroom, student-led organizations and service opportunities allow you to connect with diverse communities, both locally and globally.

Whether it’s participating in groundbreaking research, exploring Baltimore, or enjoying downtime with peers at campus wellness events, you’ll find a sense of belonging and purpose here.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: It is recommended that students have a valid driver's license and a vehicle of their own. Johns Hopkins students are responsible for providing their own transportation to clinical learning sites in Baltimore and surrounding communities (20-30 miles from the School of Medicine). How a current student decides to manage their round-trip travel is a personal decision, and they should plan accordingly. For fairness to all students, transportation is not taken into account for site assignments.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Johns Hopkins has again pushed the study of medicine forward with introducing the Johns Hopkins Genes to Society curriculum. The Genes to Society curriculum presents a model of health and disease based on the principles of adaptation to the environment, variability of the genotype, and stratification of risk, rather than simply a dichotomous view of "normal human biology (health)" and "abnormal physiology (disease)."

The curriculum provides sound foundations in basic sciences and clinical medicine while retaining the flexibility required for students to identify and develop diverse career interests. Instead of letter grades, the grading system is pass/fail. Third and fourth-year students' grades are currently pass/fall for required clerkships and honors, high pass, pass or fail for sub-internships and advanced clinical electives. The M.D. program includes the integration of basic sciences and clinical experiences and the expanded use of case-based, small-group learning sessions. Students learn the medical interview and basic physical examination in the first months of medical school and work with community physicians' practices through years 1 and 2. For more information, visit: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/som/curriculum/genes-to-society
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The School of Medicine offers a primary care education track for students specifically interested in primary care. Students do not have to apply for the primary track: it is something they may elect to choose after they have matriculated.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Nearly 2,000 different studies take place on the Hopkins campus. More than half of our clinical faculty are working on research funded by the National Institutes of Health. Medical students aren't required to take on research projects, but more than 80 percent of them do.  These may range from two month electives to a year or more of leave for extended studies. Students learn to regard research in its broadest sense. To learn more, please visit: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/som/offices/research-scholarship
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Some of the courses are time-limited and others appear throughout the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: SOURCE is the community engagement and service-learning center that supports a wide variety of community engagement opportunities through partnerships with 100+ non-profit organizations in Baltimore.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Exceptional research opportunities are available. All students must do a scholarly concentration, which can be research-based. Nearly 99% of students have done research by the time they graduate.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Johns Hopkins Bayview, Howard County General Hospital (Columbia, MD), Sibley Memorial Hospital (Washington, D.C.), Suburban Hospital (Bethesda, MD), All Children's Hospital (St. Petersburg, FL)
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: The grading system is pass/fail. Third and fourth-year students' grades are pass/fall for required clerkships and honors, high pass, pass or fail for sub-internships and advanced clinical electives.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, founded in 1893, is a private, nondenominational institution which fosters the training of medical practitioners, teachers, and biomedical scientists. The medical center provides library facilities, off-campus housing assistance, cafeterias, recreational sports in the Cooley Center, and performing arts programs. Preclinical courses are taught in the Armstrong Medical Education Building. Medical care facilities such as the Johns Hopkins Hospital and the Outpatient Center provide an extensive and diverse patient base for the teaching of all clinical subjects. Students also attend educational programs conducted at community hospitals in Baltimore and pursue elective experiences at other medical schools in the U.S. and foreign countries.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine is to prepare physicians to practice compassionate clinical medicine of the highest standard and to identify and solve fundamental questions in the mechanisms, prevention and treatment of disease, in health care delivery and in the basic sciences.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes, for admitted students who choose to attend the School of Medicine.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: In addition to those letters required for application to the MD Program, two additional letters of recommendation are required for all MD-PhD applicants. These letters are typically from faculty with whom the applicant has done research.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Committee letter: Authored by a pre-health committee or advisor and intended to represent your institution's evaluation of you. A committee letter may or may not include additional letters written in support of your application; - OR -
    Letter packet: A packet or set of letters assembled and distributed by your institution, often by the institution's career center. - OR -
    Two (2) letters from faculty members in science departments who taught you are required if the college/university you have attended does not have a Committee/Advisor AND one (1) letter from a non-science faculty member who has taught you. In addition to the letters, applicants with advanced degrees or significant postgraduate work experience of one year or more, are required to send recommendations from each component of their education and major work experience.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interviews will be conducted virtually and scheduled from September through March. Each MD candidate invited to interview will complete two interviews with a committee member (1 faculty and 1 student). We also provide an optional meet & greet with current Hopkins students every Wednesday evening before the interview day as well as a 4th year medical student panel during the lunch hour on the interview day.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: We typically begin sending interview invitations in September.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Each MD or MD/MBA applicant receives two interviews. MD-PhD applicants receive 5 interviews.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All verified AMCAS applicants receive a secondary.

medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee reviews each application holistically and considers multiple factors, including the distance traveled by the applicant.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: A holistic review process is used to select applicants to interview at Hopkins and many factors are considered in this review. These factors include the rigor of the applicant’s course of studies, grades, MCAT scores, clinical and research exposure, letters of recommendation, personal statement and the applicant’s understanding of medicine. In addition, we consider the path the applicants have taken which led to their desire to apply to medical school and become a physician.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Johns Hopkins School of Medicine is committed to providing financial assistance to all eligible students who qualify based on the availability of funds and demonstrated financial need. In the fall of 2024, Johns Hopkins began offering medical students full cost-of-attendance financial aid packages (including tuition, living expenses, and fees) to families earning less than $175,000. Additionally, families earning less than $300,000 will receive scholarships covering tuition costs. We work with each student to explore options for making a Johns Hopkins medical education possible. All federal and institutional awards administered through the Financial Aid Office are based on demonstrated financial need. To determine financial need, students must complete the CSS Profile application for institutional scholarship funding (parental information required). Students considering federal aid must also complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). All students applying to the School of Medicine may apply for financial aid assistance. However, students must meet specific citizenship requirements, be in good academic standing, and complete all required application forms to be considered for aid. 

Financial aid funding is available to all current and newly admitted non-US resident medical students. Johns Hopkins Medicine International has funded the JHM International Scholarship Program. It aims to help nurture the next generation of healthcare leaders and reduce the financial burden that non-US resident students may face when seeking funding for medical education.  Students may also apply for private loan financing. 

Our indebted graduates' average medical school debt is in the lowest decile of all medical schools in the country, and 85% of students who apply for financial aid receive some form of financial assistance to help pay their educational expenses.

To learn more about financial aid, please visit: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/som/offices/finaid

In addition to funding support, the Financial Aid Office offers financial planning, debt management counseling, and workshop services to help students manage their loan borrowing and make informed decisions about their economic well-being. Additional information can be found online by visiting: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/som/offices/finaid/debt-mgmt

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Admitted applicants should narrow their acceptances to three medical schools by this date.
By April 30,  admitted applicants must narrow their choice to one medical school using the "Plan to Enroll" tool or the "Commit to Enroll" tool.
Admitted applicants who decide to enroll at Hopkins must "Commit to Enroll" by June 15, 2026. Note: final date to be determined.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: If placed on the Waiting List (WL), the candidate must return a form to remain on the WL by late April. The admissions committee will begin to contact WL candidates on a rolling basis May-June.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Applicants must have 8 semester hours each of Biology (w/lab), General Chemistry (w/lab) & Physics (w/lab), and 4 semester hours of Organic Chemistry (w/lab), & 3 or 4 semester hours of Biochemistry (lab not required). Also, 6 to 8 semester hours of Calculus or Statistics & 24 semester hours of Humanities, Social and/or Behavioral Sciences.  Two of the Humanities courses must have been writing intensive courses. Advanced Placement (AP) & International Baccalaureate credits acceptable to the student's undergraduate college may be used to satisfy the prerequisites in Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Calculus/Statistics & up to one-half of the Humanities/Social, and Behavioral Sciences.  If using AP or IB credit for Biology, an additional semester in Advanced Biology, such as Cell Biology, Genetics, Physiology, Molecular Biology, etc., is required. If using AP or IB credit for General Chemistry, an additional semester in Advanced Chemistry (such as a second semester of Organic Chemistry).
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No expiration date. Individuals who have not completed their studies in Biology within the past four years are strongly encouraged to take an additional course in Mammalian or Molecular Biology.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: A Bachelor's degree is required in addition to proven academic competence, strong communications skills, previous achievements and activities help the Committee on Admissions to evaluate applicants' suitability for medicine. Applicants who have unusual talents, strong humanistic qualities, demonstrated leadership, and significant experience requiring teamwork skills, and creative abilities, are sought. There are no residency requirements and international students are encouraged to apply. Passage of TOEFL is required for all students whose undergraduate instruction was conducted in a language other than English. Students matriculating at Hopkins are required to undergo a criminal background check. Due to space limitations, Hopkins does not admit transfer students. JHU complies with federal and state laws prohibiting discrimination.
